title: Priority-fused signal queue and noise-adaptive throttling for usage/cost/latency alerts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a backend service that ingests fused usage/cost/latency signals, scores event priority via a lightweight pulse model, and enqueues candidate notifications into a rate-aware delivery queue with adaptive suppression. Goal: reduce noisy duplicate alerts and false positives for tenants while guaranteeing high-priority incidents reach on-call within SLA. This complements existing anomaly detectors by acting as a final deliverability filter and cadence manager in the Console alerting pipeline.
background: Current pipeline emits many correlated anomalies (same root cause surface across usage, cost, and tail-latency) which triggers multiple alerts and fatigues teams. Existing suppression is static (fixed dedup windows) and doesn't account for tenant exposure, signal provenance, or downstream delivery capacity (PagerDuty/Slack). We need a dynamic layer that fuses correlated alerts, scores them, and controls delivery cadence based on system and customer impact.
goals: Fuse correlated metrics into single actionable notices when appropriate
Prioritize alerts by customer exposure and quality score
Apply adaptive suppression windows that shrink/grow based on signal volatility and historical false-positive rate
Respect delivery quotas and backpressure from notification providers
non_goals: Replace core anomaly detectors; this is a downstream firmware layer
Solve long-term model drift - initial approach should be lightweight and interpretable
design_summary: Pipeline stages: (1) Ingest candidate anomalies from anomaly bus (Kafka topic: anomaly.events). (2) Enrich with tenant metadata, recent traffic, and cost exposure via enrichment service. (3) Run 'pulse' scorer - rule-weighted features (signal overlap, z-score magnitude, tenant exposure, recent alert churn) to compute priority and confidence. (4) Push into a priority-fused queue that enforces per-tenant delivery rate limits and global send concurrency. (5) Adaptive throttler adjusts suppression windows and escalation policy based on short-term false-positive telemetry and downstream delivery latency.
data_flow: Enrichment: tenant-lookup/cost-lookup/cache (Redis) + recent telemetry window (TSDB query)
Queue: priority-fused-queue (RabbitMQ or Redis streams) with per-tenant tokens
sample_detector_query: SELECT tenant_id, metric, anomaly_score, event_ts FROM anomaly_events WHERE event_ts > now() - interval '1 hour' AND anomaly_score > 3;
sample_scoring_logic: priority = round( 0.4 * normalized_anomaly_score + 0.3 * normalized_cost_exposure + 0.2 * tenant_slo_risk + 0.1 * recent_alert_churn ); confidence = sigmoid(raw_model_sum); apply minimum confidence threshold 0.5 for immediate delivery
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end: injected synthetic correlated anomalies result in a single fused notification for the same root cause 80%+ of test runs
False positives: suppression reduces tenant-visible duplicate notifications by >= 60% on historical spike runs
SLO: delivery latency (enqueue->delivery) 99th <= 45s under normal load
Observability: dashboards for the telemetry_metrics_to_track exist and alert on regressions
Graceful fallback: if scoring service fails, system falls back to conservative dedup window and continues delivering
tasks: Prototype pulse-scorer (rule-based) and run offline on 30d historical events
Implement enrichment cache for tenant exposure with TTL and tap for manual overrides
Create priority-fused-queue abstraction with token bucket per tenant
Add adaptive suppression controller with simple heuristics and experiment flags
Integrate delivery capacity feedback from notifier (rate-limited responses) into suppression decisions
Instrument dashboards and create alert rules for the new telemetry metrics
Run canary for 2 non-prod orgs then 3 pilot customers before wide rollout
risks_and_mitigation: Over-suppression causing missed critical alerts -> mitigation: conservative thresholds + mandatory escalation for P0s
Latency overhead at scoring/enrichment -> mitigation: cache hot paths and circuit-breaker to bypass scoring if >300ms
Model/heuristic regressions -> mitigation: shadow mode and A/B comparison before flip
Downstream integration rate limits -> mitigation: token bucket with prioritized replenishment for high-priority events
rollout_plan: Stage 1: shadow mode for 14 days (no user-facing suppression) on 100% of traffic to gather metrics
Stage 2: Opt-in for pilot tenants (feature flag) and measure false positive reduction for 2 weeks
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 50% tenants with weekly monitors and rollback hooks
Stage 4: Default enable with kill-switch and runbook documented
alert_playbook: If alerts.suppressed.count spikes > 2x baseline: check pulse-scorer health and recent rule changes
If alerts.latency.ms 99th > 60s: throttle scoring median (flip circuit) and escalate to oncall@infra
If downstream_delivery_failures.count > 5%: reduce per-tenant tokens and notify integrations team
If customer complaints > 3 in 24h: disable adaptive suppression for affected tenant and open postmortem
